obs: "Because we decide that the existence of the Act itself obviates exercise of the common-law right in this case"
Northwest Airlines, Inc. v. Transport Workers Union

"Thus, once Congress addresses a subject, even a subject previously governed by federal common law, the justification for lawmaking by the federal courts is greatly diminished. Thereafter, the task of the federal courts is to interpret and apply statutory law, not to create common law."

"There is no interstice here to be filled by federal common law: overflows are covered by the Act and have been addressed by the regulatory regime established by the Act." ... "The question is whether the field has been occupied, not whether it has been occupied in a particular manner."

"[W]e remained aware \"that new federal laws and new federal regulations may in time pre-empt the field of federal common law of nuisance.\""; and "we held that the comprehensive regulatory regime created by the 1972 amendments pre-empted Illinois' federal common law remedy."
